## Introduction This vignette guides you through the process of reproducing and analyzing occurrence data for the **Gouldian Finch** in Australia. The data is sourced from the [Atlas of Living Australia (ALA)](https://www.ala.org.au/), cleaned, enriched with weather information, and visualized. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Load Required Packages and Utilities Required functions are included in `vignette-utils.R`, which you can load using: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} source("vignette-utils.R") ``` ::: You can modify this script here:\ `ecotourism/vignettes/vignette-utils.R` ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Define Global Parameters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism_name <- "gouldian_finch" organism_title <- "Gouldian Finch" taxa <- "Gouldian finch" start <- 2014 end <- 2024 email <- "your_email@email.com" ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 1: Download and Prepare Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism <- obs_data(taxa, start, end, your_email=email) |> polished_data() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 2: Save Cleaned Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mysave(organism_name, organism) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 3: Attach Nearest Weather Station ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} attach_nearest_station(organism_name) ``` ::: This enriches the dataset by adding weather station id as `ws_id`. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 4: Load and Preview Final Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} load("../data/gouldian_finch.rda") glimpse(gouldian_finch) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Data Analysis We now explore the cleaned dataset in more detail. ### Preview Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism <- myload(organism_name) organism |> glimpse() ``` ::: ### Occurrence by State ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> my_count(scientificName, obs_state, f=1) |> as_tibble() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Visualization ### Spatial Distribution Map ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> plot_map1(color_by = scientificName) ``` ::: ### Weekly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> plot_bar_week() organism |> plot_bar_week_100() ``` ::: ### Monthly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> plot_bar_month() ``` ::: ### Yearly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> plot_bar_year() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Weather Station Mapping ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} attach_nearest_station(organism_name) organism <- myload(organism_name) organism |> glimpse() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### State-wise Weather Matching Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summarize_state_frequencies(organism_name) ``` ::: **Interpretation:** - **Queensland**:\ 77 observations; 81 matched with QLD stations. - **Western Australia**:\ 951 observations; 989 matched with WA stations (some from other states). ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Pattern Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_monthly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name) plot_weekly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name) plot_seasonal_occurrence_polar(organism_name) plot_monthly_occurrence_map(organism_name) plot_monthly_occurrence_map_by_state(organism_name) plot_monthly_distribution_map(organism_name) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Conclusion You now know how to: - Access and clean Gouldian Finch occurrence data from ALA - Attach weather metadata - Analyze and visualize patterns by time and location This reproducible approach supports ecological exploration and data-driven insights for ecotourism. ##
